axes.name: Sprint Goal & Planning
axes.description: How clearly the team plans toward a shared sprint goal.

questions.text: We have a clear Sprint Goal that guides our trade-offs during the sprint.
Sprint Planning produces a plan the whole team believes in, not a list handed to us.
We plan to realistic capacity and rarely stuff the sprint full.
We finish sprints with the Sprint Goal achieved, not just items ticked off.

axes.name: Daily Scrum & Flow
axes.description: Whether the daily scrum keeps work flowing toward the goal.

questions.text: Our daily scrum helps us re-plan the day together, not report status to one person.
We focus the daily scrum on progress toward the Sprint Goal.
Blockers raised in the daily scrum get owned and followed up.
We swarm on the most important work rather than each holding our own lane.

axes.name: Review & Stakeholders
axes.description: Whether the sprint review is a real conversation with stakeholders.

questions.text: Our sprint review is a real working conversation with stakeholders, not a one-way demo.
Stakeholders give us useful feedback that reshapes the backlog.
We show a genuinely usable increment at review, not unfinished work dressed as done.
The right stakeholders show up to the review and engage with what we built.

axes.name: Retrospective & Improvement
axes.description: Whether retrospectives surface honest issues and produce real change.

questions.text: Our retrospectives surface honest issues without blame.
We commit to a small number of specific, owned improvement actions each retro.
Actions from retros actually get done before the next one.
We track whether our improvement actions are making things better.

axes.name: Backlog & Product Ownership
axes.description: Whether the backlog is ready, ordered, and owned with intent.

questions.text: The top of our backlog is refined and ready before planning.
Our Product Owner is available and decisive when we need direction.
Our backlog is clearly ordered by value, not a dumping ground.
We share a clear understanding of why each top item matters.

axes.name: Increment & Definition of Done
axes.description: Whether each sprint produces a real, releasable increment.

questions.text: We have a clear Definition of Done that the whole team shares and applies.
Each sprint we produce a usable, potentially releasable increment.
Work marked "done" rarely bounces back as incomplete or defective.
Our Definition of Done covers quality, not just feature completion.
